M1-T3.title: Define the typed trace contract: Run, Agent, Message, ToolCall, Event
tests_added: src/types/trace.test.ts — 8 tests: the ingest constant is pinned to exactly 'agent_messages' and EVENT_KINDS is exactly ['run_start','run_end','message','tool_call']; a full Run + Agent/Message/ToolCall/Event fixture is attached with `satisfies` so any renamed/dropped required field breaks compilation; broadcast is modelled as to===null; a tool call may stand alone (messageId===null); the isMessageEvent/isToolCallEvent/isLifecycleEvent guards narrow correctly and only for their own kind; each narrowed arm carries its precise member shape (expectTypeOf); the union is exhaustively switchable on `kind` with no default arm; ordering fields (at/sequence/seed) are integers so the timeline is a total order
M1-T3.verification: npm run verify green end-to-end — lint 0w/0e (--deny-warnings); format:check clean; typecheck clean; test 18/18 passed (4 files, +8 new); build green (366ms)
M1-T3.notes: The trace contract every other module speaks is now typed in src/types/ (pure data, zero deps — no three.js, no DOM, no clock, so it is jsdom-safe and importable everywhere). Declared the five PRD-mandated entities: Agent (with a derived parentId fan-out link, precomputed send/receive counts, per-agent token/cost attribution), Message (from/to with to===null as broadcast, raw body kept alongside a decoded MessagePayload + mirrored action, status, epoch-ms `at`), ToolCall (agent-attributed, messageId nullable, args/duration/cost), and Event as a discriminated union on `kind` over run_start | run_end | message | tool_call, each arm carrying a precise payload plus the shared deterministic ordering pair (`at` epoch-ms + `sequence`). Run ties them together with a required `seed` (determinism is a product requirement per PRD §5, so the layout seed is part of the contract) and a precomputed RunMeta for the HUD. Design choices that matter downstream: (1) ids and `sequence` are DERIVED from the trace, never random — that is what lets M1-T5 pin byte-identical output and M2 render a stable shape; (2) all timestamps are numbers (epoch ms), never strings/Dates, so ordering is total and timezone-free; (3) NO layout coordinates live here — the contract carries facts only, layout is M2's derived output; (4) TraceSource is a one-member union pinned to 'agent_messages' with a note not to widen it before M6-T5 (single-format ingest rule). Deliberately did NOT build the parser (M1-T4) or the normalization/counting pass (M1-T5) — this task defines shapes only; the Agent/Run counts in the contract are fields the later passes will populate. Chose const-unions over TS enums because tsconfig sets erasableSyntaxOnly. NEXT: M1-T4 (agent_messages export adapter: Supabase rows -> trace contract).

M1-T4.title: `agent_messages` export adapter (Supabase rows → trace contract)
tests_added: src/adapter/agentMessages.test.ts — 26 tests. Mapping: every row → a Message; a JSON body is decoded into a payload with the raw body preserved; to_agent NULL is modelled as to === null (broadcast); an unparseable/NULL body stays raw text with payload + action null; an out-of-enum status coerces to 'unread'; an action-bearing message yields a ToolCall whose args are the payload minus `action`; agents are derived from from_agent/to_agent with correct send/receive counts (a broadcast counts per recipient) and an involvement-based first/last-seen window; the run is bracketed by run_start/run_end with a contiguous 0-based sequence; every event attributes to a known agent or the lifecycle; JSON-text and {data}/{agent_messages}-wrapper inputs parse identically; label/seed/runId overrides are honoured; an empty export yields a valid empty Run. Determinism: two parses are byte-identical (JSON.stringify equality); a reversed/shuffled export yields the identical Run; the derived id + seed are stable per export and differ across exports. Invalid input: non-JSON text, a non-array JSON value, a non-object row, a missing from_agent/id, an unparseable created_at and duplicate primary keys all raise TraceParseError. Helpers: agentIdFor/messageIdFor/toolCallIdFor derivation and decodePayload's JSON-object-only decoding (arrays, primitives, garbage, '' and null all → null).
M1-T4.verification: npm run lint clean (0 warnings / 0 errors, 15 files); npm run typecheck clean; npm run test 44/44 passed (5 files, +26 new); npm run build green (437ms); prettier --check clean on the 3 new files
M1-T4.notes: The ONE v1 ingest path is now real. parseAgentMessagesExport (src/adapter/) turns a recorded Supabase agent_messages export — JSON text or an already-parsed row array, and it unwraps a {data}/{rows}/{agent_messages} REST-style body — into a normalized Run from src/types/ (M1-T3). Pure: no network, no clock, no DOM, no three.js, so it is jsdom-safe and importable anywhere. Mapping: each row → a Message (to_agent NULL ⇒ to === null broadcast; body kept verbatim and decoded into a MessagePayload when it is a JSON object; action mirrored for fast grouping; status coerced read/unread; created_at → epoch ms via Date.parse). When the decoded payload carries an action it ALSO yields a ToolCall (id tc_<rowId>, agent = sender, args = payload minus `action`, durationMs null, costUsd 0) — v1 rows have no spawn/tool columns, so the declared action is the only tool signal available; both surface as MessageEvent / ToolCallEvent, bracketed by one run_start ... run_end pair with a contiguous 0-based sequence. Agents are derived from the distinct from_agent/to_agent names (alphabetically ordered for a stable array) with messagesSent, messagesReceived (a broadcast counts per recipient — every agent except its sender), an involvement-based first/last-seen window (a message counts for BOTH sender and recipient), and 0 tokens/cost because v1 carries none — never invented. DETERMINISM IS THE POINT (PRD §5): rows are canonically ordered by created_at then row id BEFORE anything is derived and duplicate primary keys are rejected, so the same export parses byte-identically and a shuffled export yields the identical Run (both pinned by tests); the run id and layout seed are hashed (FNV-1a) from the normalized messages, so identical input ⇒ identical id/seed and a different input ⇒ a different, stable one. Deliberately NOT done here (kept out of scope so the adapter stays a mechanical row→contract map): role inference and the fan-out/handoff/parentage edge model, which are M2-T4 — every Agent.role is 'unknown' and every parentId is null at this stage — and the deeper normalization/hardening pass, which is M1-T5. Malformed input is rejected with a typed TraceParseError (bad JSON, a non-array value, a non-object row, a missing from_agent/id, an unparseable created_at, a duplicate id) rather than silently dropped, so a corrupt export fails loudly. NEXT: M1-T5 (TraceModel normalization pass with deterministic output + tests).

M1-T5.title: TraceModel normalization pass with deterministic output + tests
tests_added: src/model/traceModel.test.ts — 22 tests. Canonical shape: a normalized adapter Run is reproduced byte-for-byte; normalization is a fixed point; Event.sequence is contiguous 0-based in canonical order; agents sort by id and messages/tool calls by (at, id); every derived field (per-agent counts, span, RunMeta) is recomputed, so a deliberately-corrupted input normalizes back to the truth; role/parentId are preserved for M2-T4; an empty run normalizes to itself; the input is not mutated. Determinism: byte-identical across calls; unchanged when every array is reversed AND every sequence zeroed; m_9 precedes m_10 (natural id order). compareModelIds: digit runs compared numerically, the rest lexically. Integrity: unknown sender, unknown recipient, tool call with an unknown agent, tool call referencing an unknown message, an agent-attributed lifecycle event, an absent/unknown message-event agent, a message event whose mirror disagrees with its message, duplicate ids in all four collections, and a non-finite timestamp all throw TraceModelError.
M1-T5.verification: npm run lint clean (0 warnings / 0 errors, 18 files); npm run typecheck clean; npm run test 66/66 passed (6 files, +22 new); npm run build green (347ms); prettier --check clean on the 3 new files
M1-T5.notes: The pure data layer now has its normalization seam. normalizeTrace (src/model/) turns ANY Run-shaped object into a TraceModel — a Run with every contract invariant enforced — and is the single place those promises are pinned (src/types/trace.ts states the normalizer owns Event.sequence). It does four things: (1) CANONICALIZES ORDER — agents by id, messages/toolCalls by (at, id), events by (at, kind-rank, id) via a natural comparator so m_9 sorts before m_10 (a plain lexical sort would not); (2) ASSIGNS Event.sequence as a contiguous 0-based index over that canonical order; (3) RECOMPUTES every derived/precomputed field from the facts — per-agent send/receive counts, the involvement-based active window, token/cost attribution (a broadcast counts per recipient), the startedAt/endedAt span and the whole RunMeta — so a stale count in the input cannot survive; (4) VALIDATES referential integrity (unique ids; every message/tool-call/event reference resolves; lifecycle events unattributed and message/tool-call events attributed; a message event agrees with its message) and throws a typed TraceModelError rather than silently repairing a broken run. DETERMINISM IS THE DELIVERABLE (PRD §5): the model is byte-identical across calls AND independent of the input's array order and its sequence values — pinned by a test that reverses every array and zeroes every sequence and still expects byte-equality — and normalizeTrace is a fixed point. Composition is pinned too: normalizing an adapter-produced Run reproduces it byte-for-byte, so the recomputation provably agrees with the adapter's derivation. Deliberately NOT done here: re-deriving Agent.role/parentId (the M2-T4 edge model owns them, so they are preserved as-is), the fixtures (M1-T6) and the timeline/playhead (M1-T7). No coordinates, no three.js, no clock — pure and jsdom-tested; nothing about the look is asserted (human-held M5-T5). NEXT: M1-T6 (deterministic trace fixtures: fan-out, loop, dead branch, handoff chain).

M1-T6.title: Deterministic trace fixtures: synthetic runs (fan-out, loop, dead branch, handoff chain)
tests_added: src/fixtures/traceFixtures.test.ts — 25 tests. Registry: exactly the four documented shapes in stable order; every fixture is a fully-formed TraceFixture whose run is a normalized TraceModel with source 'agent_messages', label 'fixture: <title>' and messageCount equal to its row count; row ids are unique; the registry and each fixture's rows are frozen. Determinism: building a fixture twice is byte-identical (rows + run); the registry equals a fresh build; each run is a fixed point of normalizeTrace; parsing the rows REVERSED yields the identical run; every run starts at the one fixed epoch (startedAt === FIXTURE_EPOCH_MS, so no clock) with durationMs === endedAt - startedAt; each run's seed is a stable, distinct non-negative integer (content-derived, never authored). Shapes: fan-out is one orchestrator → five distinct silent workers and is the widest out-degree in the set; loop is a researcher⇄critic edge repeated three times each way after a single kickoff (7 messages, 3 agents); dead-branch has exactly one terminal leaf (worker_dead receives one message, sends none, firstSeenAt === lastSeenAt) beside a worker that completes; handoff-chain is the directed path a→b→c→d with terminating ends and a 'handoff' action on every link. Isolation: buildFixture returns fresh rows/run distinct from the registry and a mutated build does not leak into it.
M1-T6.verification: npm run verify green end-to-end — lint 0 warnings / 0 errors (21 files, --deny-warnings); format:check clean; typecheck clean; test 91/91 passed (7 files, +25 new); build green (341ms); prettier --write clean on the 3 new files
M1-T6.notes: The reference runs the rest of the build lays out, renders and compares now exist. src/fixtures/ (pure, zero-dep, jsdom-safe) exposes FIXTURE_SHAPES, buildFixture(shape) and the FIXTURES registry — four synthetic runs, one per structural shape the product is about: fan-out, loop, dead-branch, handoff-chain. The design rule that matters: a fixture is NOT a hand-built Run — it is a synthetic agent_messages ROW LIST fed through the REAL two-stage pipeline (parseAgentMessagesExport M1-T4 then normalizeTrace M1-T5), so a fixture exercises exactly the path a recorded export takes and cannot drift from it; the shape lives entirely in the message graph (the thing M2-T4's derived edge model will read), and every Agent.role/parentId is therefore left 'unknown'/null exactly as the adapter leaves them — nothing is hand-placed. Determinism (PRD §5) is the deliverable: every id, subject and JSON body is a constant and every timestamp is measured from ONE fixed epoch (FIXTURE_EPOCH_MS = 2026-10-01T09:00:00Z via iso(offset), never Date.now()), so the same shape builds byte-identical rows and run every call; the run seed/run id are left content-derived by the adapter, not authored. Each fixture is minimal and single-purpose so a downstream test failure names its shape: fan-out = orchestrator → 5 workers (maxFanOut 5, the widest in the set), loop = researcher⇄critic ×3 cycles after a kickoff (a repeating edge), dead-branch = one completing worker beside one terminal leaf that receives and never replies (firstSeenAt === lastSeenAt), handoff-chain = a→b→c→d relay. buildFixture returns a FRESH copy each call (rows are frozen) so a test may mutate its own build without corrupting the shared registry; the registry itself is frozen. Deliberately NOT done here: no layout (M2), no derived edges/roles/parents (M2-T4), no timeline (M1-T7), no render (M3), and no combined 'kitchen-sink' fixture — the real debian2_bot fleet run is the M5-T3 dogfood and the reference run for the §7 comparison. No coordinates, no three.js, no clock — pure and jsdom-tested; nothing about the look is asserted (human-held M5-T5). NEXT: M1-T7 (timeline/playhead model over the event stream).

M1-T7.title: Timeline/playhead model over the event stream + tests
tests_added: src/timeline/timeline.test.ts — 36 tests. buildTimeline: returns a Timeline sharing the model's canonical events, agentIds in model order, startedAt/endedAt/spanMs mirroring the model; collapses the stream into distinct ascending stops (first === startedAt, last === endedAt); folds several same-instant events onto one stop; byte-identical across calls; a valid empty timeline for an empty run; does not mutate the model; ascending in-range stops for all four fixtures. frameAt: a fully-formed frame at the start (clamped elapsed, timeMs = startedAt, progress 0, atEnd false, sender AND recipient live); clamps before-start / past-end; linear progress 0->0.5->1; firedCount/cursorIndex monotonic with time and cursorIndex === firedCount-1; activeAgentIds grows across the fan-out (orchestrator+worker_alpha at 0 -> all six at end); a silent recipient-only agent counts as active (dead branch); a zero-span run is one instant (all events fired, progress 1, atEnd); empty run yields cursor -1 / 0 fired / [] / progress 0 / atEnd; deterministic and non-mutating. createPlayhead: paused at 0 on DEFAULT_SPEED 1; clamps an initial position; honours options. Controls: setPlaying/setSpeed identity when unchanged; togglePlay round-trips; cycleSpeed walks the preset ladder both ways with wrapping ([2,4,0.25,0.5,1] up, [0.5,0.25,4,2,1] down); no input mutation. seek: clamps, identity when unchanged, pure. step: forward visits every stop and no-ops at the last (per fixture); backward snaps to the run start before the first stop and steps to the previous stop; steps from an in-between position; preserves speed/playing. advance: no-op when paused or delta<=0; delta scaled by speed (1000ms@1x=1000, @2x=2000); clamps at the span and auto-pauses at the end; keeps playing short of the end; deterministic. Purity guard: the module source (comments stripped) makes no Date.now( / performance.now( / Math.random( call.
M1-T7.verification: npm run lint clean (0 warnings / 0 errors, 24 files, --deny-warnings); npm run typecheck clean; npm run test 127/127 passed (8 files, +36 new); npm run build green (365ms); prettier --check clean repo-wide on the touched files
M1-T7.notes: The pure playback seam of the data layer (PRD §5 names it beside the trace contract/parser/normalization/layout) now exists in src/timeline/ — pure, zero-dep, jsdom-safe, no clock, no randomness, no mutation. buildTimeline(model) flattens a normalized TraceModel into a Timeline: the canonical events (shared, read-only), the distinct event times as `stops` (several events at one instant collapse to one stop and fire together — what makes stepping total over sub-millisecond bursts), agentIds in canonical order, and startedAt/endedAt/spanMs. frameAt(timeline, elapsedMs) is the per-frame query the render layer rides on: it clamps the position into [0, spanMs], binary-searches the last fired event (cursorIndex/firedCount), returns timeMs = startedAt+elapsed, progress, atEnd, and activeAgentIds. DESIGN DECISION: an agent is active if a fired event touches it as SENDER **or RECIPIENT** (a message fires for both ends) or as a tool-call maker — so a silent worker lights up the moment its first assignment lands, not only once it replies; that is the property the spatial scene needs to reveal fan-out/dead-branch over time, and it is why the frame scans message events for `to` rather than only reading event.agentId. activeAgentIds filters the canonical agent list (never the Set's insertion order), so it is stable. The Playhead is a plain immutable value {elapsedMs, speed, playing}; every control is a pure transition returning a new value — createPlayhead, setPlaying, togglePlay, setSpeed, cycleSpeed (walks PLAYBACK_SPEEDS = [0.25,0.5,1,2,4], wrapping, via a direction sign), seek (clamped), stepForward/stepBackward (jump to the next/previous distinct stop; forward no-ops at the last stop, backward snaps to 0 before the first), and advance(playhead, timeline, deltaMs) = elapsed += deltaMs*speed, clamped to the span and AUTO-PAUSING at the end. DETERMINISM IS THE DELIVERABLE (PRD §5): real time is passed IN as deltaMs by the caller's animation loop — the module never reads Date.now/performance.now/Math.random — so the same model+playhead always yields a byte-identical timeline/frame/playhead (pinned by JSON-equality tests), and a purity test scans the module source (comments stripped) to keep it that way. ANTI-DRIFT (PRD §8): this is the SCALAR that drives the spatial scene over time (which arcs have appeared, which nodes are hot, how far the camera has walked) and the substrate for M4-T1's scrubber — it is explicitly NOT a linear replay/search view (AgentReplay/traceview/tracediff cover that); the spatial view remains the product. Deliberately NOT done here: no layout (M2), no rendering/scrubber UI (M3/M4-T1 own the React/Zustand plumbing), no filters (M4-T5). M1 is now complete (all 7 tasks); NEXT per dependency order: M2-T1 (force-directed 3D layout over the agent graph), which depends on the completed M1-T5 + M1-T6.
